title: Early recording conditions and integrated sessions
summary: Sessions with few mics and tracks, stars recording in New Orleans, and black and white players always playing together despite stage segregation.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Did you enjoy the recording sessions? I mean that.

Yeah, yeah, yeah. That was because they didn't have all the technique that they had. And I would take one mic, you know, and they would sit up the mic like one in the other rooms. And you had to be so hard to get picked up by so many tracks on the early years I'm speaking. Yeah, two tracks. Yeah, but we had records. Right. You know, we had plenty of money for a lot of people. Because New Orleans, before Memphis thought about getting a studio, New Orleans was just slow. They didn't take advantage of what was happening, but a lot of records was coming out of New Orleans. Sure. A lot of stars, you know, at the time, Little Richard and all of the diners, all of these big stars was coming in to record. And it wasn't getting the publicity in the paper, you know, because they had the thing that they didn't want you to record the black and white, some of them, you know. And then you couldn't. Is that a problem? Yeah. Well, no, not in the studio. But on the stage, you know, on Burmese Street, you couldn't play together and all of that kind of bullshit.
When did they start having integrated sessions?
Well, there's always been integrated sessions in New Orleans because cats always play together, no matter what. We always found a way to play.
So there's never any problem with playing?

Yeah, there was a problem with, you know, some fool heard about it or something and wanted to create something. But we always played together. And what about the unions? Oh, the unions, well, they didn't do too much about it. Some of the guys that were in the union, well, we all were in the union, you know, but we would just play together. Yeah. But it was fun. Everybody didn't know who they are. So I leave it like that.
